items.note: The page opens with a header band that has a sag arc, an ink sidebar pill with a white dot, an ID-badge or person scene with crescent shading and sparkles, and a cream form panel. The parts are the reference's, but the band is about 375–440px tall and holds only an h2 title and one line. Its left half is empty and the form starts at about y=500–570, so the first screen has none of the reference's balance between text and art (02).

The phone band is compact, as in 04: a big bold title, a lead, a sag arc and an 80–90px cluster tucked into the corner. The cream panel holds a large crescent-shaded avatar disc and ink and cream pills on their ledges. Close to the reference. The section tabs are clipped at the edge (samples 1 and 3) or wrap to two loose rows (sample 2).

The night version is convincing: a navy page, an indigo band and panels, white pills with ink labels and yellow art, true to 03. Sample 3 keeps a yellow band, and the yellow-on-navy contrast is strong. As in light mode, the band is twice the height its title needs, and the form starts below the middle of the screen.

The phone band is compact in indigo or yellow, with a corner cluster, a white selected tab pill and indigo inputs on indigo panels. It reads as the 03 night palette at phone scale. In sample 3 the footer ends in a white bottom bar under the indigo footer.

The bell scenes are good. The bell is crescent-shaded, a second-hue disc cuts into it, and four-point sparkles and a cloud surround it; sample 3 sets it on a full blue band. Groups are cream panels with spot-plate icons and 1px rules. But the band is again half empty above the fold, and the off switches are pale grey tracks that almost vanish on the cream panel.

The compact band carries a bell cluster in the corner. Envelope and chat pictograms sit in white plates, and bold group titles, ruled rows and ink switches have a considered rhythm close to 07 and 09. The off switch is a near-white track on cream and reads as missing.

At night the off tracks turn indigo with a white knob and on tracks white with an ink knob, which separates far better than by day. The indigo or blue band, white plates and indigo panels follow 03. The oversized, mostly empty header band remains the main weakness.

The phone night screen is tidy: a compact indigo or blue band, a small bell cluster, white plates and ruled switch rows on indigo panels. Hierarchy is clear and the screen is close to the reference's night palette. In sample 3 the page ends in a white footer bar.

The padlock scenes name the subject at a glance, built from a shackle and a crescent-shaded body with a second-hue disc, a star and a sparkle; sample 3 adds a cloud and an ink-stroke shackle. Below them come a key plate, a ruled sessions table and cream Revoke pills with danger labels. The language is right, but the tall half-empty band pushes the password form to the middle of the screen.

The band is compact with a padlock cluster in the corner. A key plate sits beside a bold group title, and full-width inputs lead to an ink full-width pill, a faithful phone translation. Sample 3's tab strip cuts the selected tab off at the screen edge.

In the night version the white plates and indigo inputs are clean, the padlock art holds its hues, and the green band in sample 3 stays saturated, all faithful to 03. The band-height problem is the same as in light mode.

The compact night band, padlock cluster, white key plate and indigo form panel read as the reference's night palette. The sessions table scrolls inside its frame. In sample 3 the page ends in a white footer bar.

The plan cards now match the reference: borderless cream options, with the selected plan as the one saturated field (orange or violet) carrying a check disc, a spaced eyebrow and a bold price. This closes the rc.3 bordered-card gap and comes close to 08. The wallet-and-coin scene is good, but the band above the plans is still about 375px of mostly empty colour.

On the phone, the compact band leads to stacked borderless plan cards with big bold prices, an ink or white current-plan pill and green ticks, then a cream invoices panel. The rhythm is close to the reference. In sample 3 the selected section tab (Billing) is scrolled out of view.

At night, indigo unselected plans sit beside a saturated orange or violet selected plan, which separates clearly on navy, as 03 shows a bright panel on night. White switch pills carry ink labels. The tall header band again spends the top half of the screen on a title.

On the phone at night, the compact band leads to indigo plan cards and one saturated selected plan with a white check disc, so the hierarchy is clear. In sample 3 the page ends in a white bottom bar, the only light surface on the night page.

findings.summary: On desktop every settings header band is still sized by its art: about 375–440px tall, it holds only an h2 title and one line of lead in the top-left, and it leaves half the band as empty colour. The first form field, the first switch group or the plans start at about y=500–570 of a 900px viewport. The reference earns a tall band only with a full text block (a headline, lead, checklist and pill, as in 02); a band that only names the page stays short (04). The rc.4 lead review named this gap, and it holds in all three samples.
findings.promptFix: Size a compact product header band by its text, not its art. Remove the art-derived min-height, so the band is its text block plus `space.10` above and `space.8` below: about 200–260px on desktop and never more than a third of the first screen. Cap the art box at the band's inner height, in the trailing 40% of its width. Draw the scene in a wide viewBox (about 400×200) with `height: 100%; width: auto; max-width: 100%`, so it spreads sideways instead of making the band taller. Only a front-page hero that carries a display headline, a lead and pills may grow tall around its art. On any screen whose job is a form, a list of settings or a choice, the first control starts within the first 600px of a desktop viewport.
findings.specRule: .ms-field--header { --ms-arc: var(--size-arc-sm); padding-block: var(--space-10) var(--space-8); min-height: calc(min(42vw, var(--size-band-art)) * 0.6 + var(--space-12)); }

findings.summary: In light mode an off switch is a warm-grey track one step from the cream panel it sits on, so off rows look as if they had no control. The reference's controls on cream separate clearly from their panel (09). At night the indigo off track reads well.

In dark mode the one sample that renders a footer ends every page in a bright white bottom bar under the indigo footer. It is the only light surface on the night page, while the reference's night palette (03) stays dark to the edge. This was named in rc.3 and is still open.
findings.promptFix: Give the footer bottom bar its own role token, the darkest surface in both appearances: ink by day, and at night a step darker than the navy page, with white text. Keep `surface.inverse` for small floating pieces such as toasts.
findings.specRule: Footer | Cream band with rise arc, link columns, a signup field + ink pill; `surface.inverse` bottom bar with round icon buttons … (dark) `color.surface.inverse` | `#ffffff`

findings.summary: On phones the section tab strip does not keep the current tab in view. Sample 3 clips the selected tab at the right edge or scrolls it fully out of view, and sample 2 wraps the tabs into two loose rows. This is the agent's own doing; the spec does not lead to it.
